entries.heading: Model 2
paragraphs: Approx. 1878 flush frets, wooden tension pancake head.

Alfred D Cammyer came from America in approximately 1885. Started a workshop and regarded as the maker of the first zither banjos and indeed made well crafted and beautiful zither banjos. This craftsmanship also extended and evident in his open backed banjos.
At one time he did form a partnership with Clifford Essex but dissolved the partnership in 1900. Cammyer did make thousands of banjos in total always held in high esteem.

Later on Sidney Young worked with Cammyer on producing his banjos. Making banjos from 1890 onwards. Always tell a Sidney Young made instrument because of the craftsmanship as one of the finest banjo makers. Sidney Young produced banjos such as ‘The Vibrant’, ‘The Vibrant Rile’ zither banjos and then went into producing ‘new era’ banjos which were absolutely fabulous.

entries.heading: Model 1
paragraphs: This is a W. Cole banjo from around 1882 a very rare banjo and in this condition pretty unique. 1 inch pot which is the eclipse design an American maker who exported during the late 19th Century. It’s a real beauty.

Born in Birmingham, Warwickshire but moved with his family to Broughton in Lancashire 1881. He was a musical instrument maker including Organs. In 1901 he was married with two daughters living in Stockport, Cheshire and was employed as a piano tuner and instrument repairer. He had also changed the spelling of his name to Crosbie.
Crosby/Crosbie banjos are held in very high esteem and rarely come up for sale, they are the most fabulous sounding banjos for an style you wish to play.

entries.heading: Model 1
paragraphs: A killer banjo brilliant sound scale 26 inch, pot 11inch countersunk tone ring. Houghton started in Birmingham, Ludgate Hill around 1882 moved in the early 20th Century to the London area both his works were called the Reliance works. Houghton had his fingers in many pies he made some of the Clifford Essex banjos notably the popular model and the Clipper. Also made mandolins for Bel Line and Marvel, he took the franchise to make Jedson banjos after J Dallas sold up in 1943 his instrument bore the British Lion stamp on the peg heads.

This is a rare and remarkable banjo very rare made by George Morris around 1885. It is one of the most pleasurable banjos to play with fantastic tone and volume.
Scale 27inches pot 12 inches. George Morris was renowned for the quality of his banjos and anyone who has one never sells. Waited 30 years to get one!

This model has a mute through an arm rest, it’s hinged preso on the right-hand side to engage the mute. 4 studs showing in the neck raises studs to turn it into a short scale Piccolo banjo, what a marvel.

entries.heading: Model 5 Fretless early model. Stringless at present early Taylor banjo from late 19th Century. Top quality timber used in manufacture with strengthened neck to stand up to the forces applied and so very very fine.

entries.heading: Model 7
paragraphs: About 1885 it has a few thigs missing (lever operated mut system) and it’s original tuners but plays very well not bad for 135 years old.

entries.heading: Model 1
paragraphs: Tonbridgeware banjo, 6 string from around 1860. It took 3 months to refurbish, no idea of maker they were cottage industry and generally made for tourist pieces.
An example a very early English banjo unknown maker it’s around 1850 the construction is second to none it’s not finished yet in restoration but a thing of beauty.

This model is a high end late 19th Century banjo superbly made it is marked but too faint to read. 48 hooks and nuts on an 11inch and 1/2inch pot, scale 26 inch and a really nice sounding banjo. It would have been fretless but fretted in the 1920’s as so many of the Minstrel banjos were.

An old 6 string banjo from around 1860/1870. It had been altered and been through the mill but now restored. It has a big sound pot 1inch and 5/8inch no idea of maker but the banjo came from Keith Wilson and originally from the C Wicham Collection. Beautiful marquetry on the fretboard.

entries.heading: Model 1
paragraphs: Around 1894 a beauty really well made 5 string, pot is 13 inch, scale 29 inch. Wilks made banjo in the late 19th Century until around 1914. I have not come across this model before but he was based in Manchester.

entries.heading: Model 2
paragraphs: Fc Wilks applied for a patent which was granted in 1894 for this banjo design with the hole in the vellum and an enclosed back. This model is around 1900 101/4 inch pot, scale 26 inch and plays really nicely.
